runtime_boundaries_identified: Three-process split: main (Node/Electron) / sandboxed preload (contextBridge facade) / renderer (Vue), with renderer reaching Node only through window.electron/fileUtils/path/… typed in shared/types/ipc.ts.

Renderer↔main IPC surface: the four typed contract categories (invoke/send/sync/main-event); main-side handlers are still registered via bare ipcMain.on/handle in business classes and are not type-checked against the contract.
Main-process-internal dispatch: onInternalChannel / ipcMain.emit in utils/internalIpc.ts used as a pseudo-IPC bus between main modules (flagged for collapse into direct typed calls).
Window lifecycle/routing boundary: WindowManager Map<number, BaseWindow> registry with EDITOR/SETTINGS subclasses; identity mixes event.sender lookup, explicit windowId, and internal emit.

Editor engine boundary: renderer consumes @muyajs/core at source level (workspace dep, exports '.' → ./src/index.ts) behind a hand-written any shim (types/muya-core.d.ts); legacy @marktext/muyajs retired.

File write boundary: main-process-owned durable writeFile (write-file-atomic + fsync + rename) in filesystem/index.ts; save/save-as dialogs currently live in menu/actions/file.ts (flagged as a misplaced owner).

rationale: The review is unusually well-grounded: every load-bearing claim was checked against implementation, config, tests, and docs and nearly all are precise, with line-level citations that match the checkout. It correctly classifies the repo as an Electron pnpm monorepo, distinguishes current code from stale docs (ARCHITECTURE.md pre-monorepo layout / IPC.md src/ paths / CLAUDE.md 'a handful of muya call sites' — all three resolved in favor of current code), and discloses the real evidence limitation (no incremental git history, no Bash). The friction, quality-attribute ranking, three options (status quo, premature abstraction, selective consolidation), the single recommendation with per-direction stable/defer calls, and the phased reversible migration with named verification (typecheck, architecture-check script, named e2e specs, muya conformance) all satisfy the full-credit signals. The legacy JS engine packages/muyajs is correctly treated as retired, never as current. Two minor errors — an off line count (758 vs ~850) for menu/actions/file.ts and an unverified rationale for webSecurity:false — do not change the recommendation and are not material. Accuracy gate passes: 0 material errors, 0 unresolved decision-relevant conflicts.
